questions.q: What does the fallback date of "1900-01-01" handle when reading the watermark?
options: The maximum date Delta Lake allows in a partition column
The very first run against a source, when no watermark row exists yet, so everything counts as new
A corrupted watermark table that needs to be reset
A source file that was deleted after being ingested
questions.explain: When no watermark row exists yet for a source, the fallback date makes the filter treat all available data as new, which is correct since nothing has been ingested before.

questions.q: Which line in the ingestion script is specifically responsible for turning this into an incremental job rather than a full reload?
options: The .select(...) listing out the business columns
The .filter(F.col("sale_date") > F.lit(last_ingested_date)) on the source read
The .withColumn("ingested_at", F.current_timestamp()) call
The spark.read.format("csv").option("header", "true") call
questions.explain: That filter is what prevents the job from scanning or touching any data at or before the watermark -- it's the line that turns 'reprocess everything' into 'process only what's new.'

questions.q: Why is .mode("append") the correct write mode for bronze.sales_raw in this design?
options: Because append mode automatically deduplicates rows on write
Because bronze.sales_raw has no transaction_id column to match on
Because the source filter already guaranteed the incoming rows are new, so appending them is safe and correct
Because Delta Lake tables can never be overwritten under any circumstances
questions.explain: Append is safe specifically because the earlier filter on sale_date already restricted the DataFrame to rows that are new since the watermark -- Bronze stays append-only exactly like the Beginner project.

questions.q: Why must the watermark only be advanced after the Bronze append has actually succeeded?
options: Advancing it early makes the next run read MORE data than it should
It has no effect either way, since the watermark is only used for reporting
Delta Lake requires watermark updates to happen before any write, not after
Advancing it too early risks silently skipping real data if the run fails partway through
questions.explain: If the watermark moves forward before the append is confirmed, a failed run could leave a gap where data was never actually ingested but the watermark claims it was.

questions.q: What is the watermark-advance step in this lesson's code built from?
options: An UPDATE statement with no matching condition, applied to every row
A full DROP TABLE and recreate of meta.last_ingested_date on every run
A manual edit of a configuration file outside of Spark
A MERGE INTO against meta.last_ingested_date, inserting if the source is new and updating if it already exists
questions.explain: The watermark advance uses the same MERGE INTO idea used later for Silver -- insert the source if it's never been seen, update its date if it has -- just against a one-row-per-source bookkeeping table.
